learning: If oscillation is at or below 0.2 with progress above 0.4, the light inertia and kp 2.2 hold the line. If oscillation is still above 0.2, reduce kp further (to about 2.0) before any geometry change.
notes: Builder's light-robot geometry (0.6 kg, 0.12 m body, 0.10 m track, 0.03 m wheels) with the y = 0.02 m, 16 mm, seven-sensor row from iteration 5. Controller is kp 2.2 and kd 0.5, lowered and damped from iteration 3 because that light-robot run had oscillation of 0.309.
rationale: Iteration 3 (0.6 kg, 0.12 m body, 0.10 m track, y = 0.03 m, kp 2.5, kd 0.4) gave the highest oval progress of the light-robot runs (0.45) but oval steering_oscillation of 0.309, above the 0.2 threshold. Iteration 5 showed that moving the row to y = 0.02 m with the seven-sensor, 16 mm array removed slalom line loss (0 at 0.8 kg), and iteration 4 showed that the heavier robot damped oscillation (0.181) at a cost in progress (0.34). The Builder's proposal combines the light inertia with the y = 0.02 m row. I keep the geometry as proposed and take the oscillation cost as the controller's problem. The Builder's own note says that if oscillation stays above 0.2 I should reduce kp to about 2.2, so I set kp 2.2. I also raise kd from 0.4 to 0.5 for extra damping on the light robot. The sensor weights stay proportional to x (about 33 times x, with the outer sensors at +/-2), so the signal scale matches the earlier runs. ki stays at 0.05, base_speed at 1.4 and line_loss at last_direction, which gave zero line loss on the oval and s-bend in every run with those settings. Expected, not measured: oval progress 0.40 to 0.45, line_loss near 0, oscillation 0.2 to 0.3, and max_error about 0.062 m. Iterations 0 to 5 show max_error has not moved with geometry, so the remaining gap is a controller gain question.
